prompt_en: An intricate photographic scene captures a single visible action in a theatrical costume repair room. The central seamstress is a newly designed 32-year-old woman; her visible face and hair follow the supplied image: a dark chin-length bob, separated wispy fringe, dark eyes, softly tapered jaw and softly rounded lips. She stands on screen left beside a workbench, wearing a sage cotton work shirt, an ivory canvas apron and charcoal trousers. A newly designed 38-year-old male stage performer stands on screen right in a plum velvet cape over a dark jacket. She is separating a snapped gold braided cord on his cape from the top edge of her own apron, holding the interrupted repair for one attentive beat. Her right thumb and index finger pinch the top canvas edge of her own apron at her upper chest, making a small raised fold; the inner surface of her right palm and its creases face the camera. Her left forearm reaches toward the performer, and her left index finger curves visibly beneath the gold braid where it remains attached to his upper lapel. The back of her left hand faces the lens, displaying its knuckles and short nails while its palm faces his jacket. A small star brooch sits above two short frayed cord ends hanging on his cape. Her shoulders remain nearly frontal, her head turns modestly toward him, and her eyes glance back toward the lens. An asymmetric closed-mouth smile gives this brief professional pause a quietly inviting presence. Both of her wrists and connected forearms remain visible between the separate contact sites. A landscape frame includes both adult heads through upper hips; the apron clearly belongs to her and the cape stays worn by him. Warm task-lamp light falls across her face and the two hands, with garment racks and a spool tray softly receding behind them. Crisp canvas folds, velvet nap and metal glints keep the repair tactile within a restrained backstage editorial photograph.
